1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with clearly separated lines and ample white space, though letter spacing appears standard rather than explicitly enhanced.

2.why: All instructions are in sentence case with no italics or dense paragraphs; the only all-caps strings are the recovery codes and setup secret themselves, which are data, not instructions.

3.why: Every screen is a narrow single-column layout with large touch targets and short text that fits a mobile viewport without crowding.

4.why: Instructions are one-to-two short plain sentences, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code.' and 'Each code works once if you cannot use your authenticator.'

5.why: Input fields show format examples: 'Example: 123456' for identity and authenticator codes and 'Example: ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' for recovery codes, plus a sample email.

6.why: No screen contains more than two short sentences of instructional text; the longest block is the two-line QR fallback note.

7.why: Step 6 offers a 'Copy setup secret' button for the 32-character secret and steps 8-9 offer 'Copy all codes' for the recovery codes.

8.why: Step 5 displays a large scannable QR setup pattern as an alternative to the manual setup secret, with a note pointing to the manual option if scanning is difficult.

9.why: Screenshots show standard text inputs but contain no visible evidence (e.g., autocomplete attributes or password-manager prompts) confirming or denying autofill/password-manager support.

10.why: A four-segment progress bar at the top highlights the current step on every screen, and each screen has one large blue primary button.

11.why: Each screen has exactly one blue primary action, but some screens also present multiple secondary buttons (e.g., step 8 has 'Show recovery codes', 'Copy all codes', and 'Use a recovery code' alongside 'I saved my codes').

12.why: Every action produces a plain status message such as 'Identity checked. Next, set up your authenticator.', 'New recovery codes created. Save them now.', and 'Recovery code accepted and used.'

13.why: The flow provides 'Request another code', Show/Hide toggles for the QR pattern, setup secret, and recovery codes, and a 'Back?' link, with no warning or penalty text anywhere.

14.why: The only error shown, 'Your page check expired. Refresh the page and try again.', states the problem and the fix without blame, though 'page check' is mildly technical jargon.

15.why: No countdowns or reading timers appear on any screen, but the 'Your page check expired' message on steps 14-15 shows the session does expire after some period of inactivity.
